_credit: This taxonomy is absorbed from a teammate's social-media-marketing-specialist skill. Shared reference data, not personal config — intentionally not gitignored.

triggers.name: Curiosity gap
triggers.signature: Sets up a question the viewer must resolve.
triggers.example_hook: You won't believe what happens when...
triggers.use_when: The payoff is genuinely surprising or counter-expectation — don't force this if the answer is predictable, the gap collapses and the hook falls flat.

triggers.name: Fear / FOMO
triggers.example_hook: Stop doing this — it's killing your reach
triggers.use_when: There's a real, specific cost to inaction. Vague fear ('you're missing out on something') reads as manipulative; a named, concrete stake doesn't.

triggers.name: Identity signal
triggers.example_hook: If you're a [X], you already know...
triggers.use_when: The audience has a real shared identity/in-group (a niche, a role, a shared struggle) — this falls flat addressed to a generic audience.

triggers.name: Pain point
triggers.signature: Meets the viewer in their frustration.
triggers.example_hook: Tired of posting and getting zero views?
triggers.use_when: The frustration is specific and the viewer would nod immediately — generic pain points ('life is hard') don't land.

triggers.name: Transformation promise
triggers.example_hook: How I went from 0 to 100K in 60 days
triggers.use_when: There's a real, specific before/after with numbers or a concrete comparison — vague improvement claims read as generic AI-slop territory.

triggers.name: Social proof
triggers.example_hook: 1M people already watched this — here's why
triggers.use_when: The proof point is real and verifiable (an actual view count, an actual number of users) — a fabricated-sounding number undermines trust instantly.

triggers.name: Controversy / Hot take
triggers.use_when: The teammate actually holds the position and can defend it in comments — a hot take with no real conviction behind it reads as bait, not perspective.
